item.title: Believe Founders Denis Ladegaillerie & Romain Vivien Explain the Global Rise of Their Multibillion-Dollar Music Company | Billboard News
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: "Welcome to our podcast, where we explore the latest trends and success stories in the music industry. Today, we're talking to the founders of Believe, a multibillion-dollar music company that's commanding 10% of the global digital market. Let's dive in and find out what sets them apart.
[Soft music plays in the background]
Host: "Believe's founders, Denis Ladegaillerie and Romain Vivien, have outmaneuvered the major label system, attracting top musical acts like Janet Jackson, Cleo Sol, and Russ. So, what's their secret? According to Denis, their market share globally in digital music is close to 10%, which translates to tens of millions of dollars of value.
[Short clip of Denis speaking]
Denis Ladegaillerie: "We are now the No. 1 to No. 3 player in Asia, and the No. 1 to 3 players across Europe and the Middle East. Now is the right time for us to start looking at North America."
Host: "Romain Vivien attributes their success in France to their early bet on hip-hop, a genre that was quick to adopt digital music and streaming. This allowed Believe to stay agile and adapt to the changing market.
[Short clip of Romain speaking]
Romain Vivien: "A hip-hop artist produces music every six months, whereas a pop artist releases an album every three, four, five years. We need to stay agile to meet the needs of the artist ecosystem and the markets."
Host: "Believe's business model allows artists to retain master ownership while leveraging a massive global infrastructure. It's no wonder top acts are flocking to their platform. Tune in next time for more insights into the music industry. Thanks for listening!"
[Outro music plays]
